name_story.story: Aziah can be understood through the Arabic form عَزِيَّة, whose central sense is aziah; mighty, dear (feminine) (malay form). Aziah is the Malay form of Arabic عَزِيَّة (ʿAziyya), the feminine of عَزِيز, meaning 'mighty, dear'.

faq.a: Aziah is associated with the Arabic form عَزِيَّة, whose core sense is aziah; mighty, dear (feminine) (malay form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Aziah?
faq.a: Aziah is associated with Arabic. Aziah is the Malay form of Arabic عَزِيَّة (ʿAziyya), the feminine of عَزِيز, meaning 'mighty, dear'.
Yes — the underlying form عَزِيَّة is Arabic.
Aziah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Aziah should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿAziyya is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Aziah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Aziah is rendered عزیہ and carries the sense عزیہ، پیاری.

faq.q: What does Aziah mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Aziah is rendered عزیه and carries the sense عزیه، عزیز.
A romanized syllable approximation is a-ziah. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Aziah?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Aziah, aziah. Script forms are عزيه, عزیه, عزیہ, عَزِيَّة, अज़िया.

faq.q: Is Aziah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
